ai_summary: AI blamed inter-VLAN routing because remote networks failed.
human_correction: Evidence showed the PC gateway was 192.168.10.254 while the router gateway was 192.168.10.1.
why_it_matters: A routing fix would not repair a bad client gateway.

ai_summary: AI suggested the router subinterface was down.
human_correction: The DHCP binding showed clients were receiving 192.168.6.0/24 addresses for a 192.168.60.0/24 VLAN.
why_it_matters: Interface state was not the fault; DHCP pool network was wrong.

ai_summary: AI said ACL 101 blocked all traffic.
human_correction: ACL 101 permitted one subnet but omitted required permits for other subnets, causing implicit deny.
why_it_matters: The fix must add specific permits, not simply delete security policy.

human_correction: Static NAT mapped 203.0.113.50 to 192.168.10.5 instead of the web server 192.168.10.50.
why_it_matters: The service was reachable internally; the translation target was wrong.

human_correction: Wireless clients got addresses from guest VLAN 99, proving the WLAN-to-VLAN mapping was wrong.
why_it_matters: Adding DHCP addresses would expand the wrong network.
